rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should establish a baseline for RNA-only single-profile models using PCA encoding. This tests the fundamental performance of RNA data alone, isolating the impact of the RNA encoder and profile setting. It clarifies whether RNA-only models can achieve reasonable accuracy, providing critical evidence for later comparisons with multimodal or image-only approaches.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (RNA-only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) achieves 0.4849 accuracy. This experiment tests the impact of switching the RNA encoder to scvi_n200 while keeping other settings identical (singleprofile, no image encoder, no aggregation). This isolates the effect of the RNA encoder choice, a critical design decision, and provides direct comparison to determine if scvi_n200 improves performance over pca_n2000 in the same baseline setup.

Existing evidence shows scvi_n200 (config_004) outperforms pca_n2000 (config_001) for rna_only models. This experiment tests whether multiprofile (profile_setting) with aggregation=avgpool improves performance using the better RNA encoder (scvi_n200). It isolates the impact of profile setting and aggregation, which are critical design choices with sparse prior evidence.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings with aggregation (avgpool) significantly outperform singleprofile (config_005 vs config_001). scvi_n200 (config_004) is better than pca_n2000 for singleprofile. This experiment tests whether transformer aggregation (vs avgpool) further improves performance with scvi_n200 in multiprofile, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It balances exploitation (building on multiprofile success) and exploration (testing aggregation variants).

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only multiprofile models with scvi_n200 and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy (0.653). This experiment tests whether switching to scgpt RNA encoder (a different representation) while keeping the same aggregation method isolates the impact of the RNA encoder on performance. This is critical for understanding if scgpt offers better representation for multiprofile data, without confounding factors from other design choices.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only multiprofile models with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation achieve high accuracy (0.653). This experiment tests adding image data (resnet50) to this strong baseline, isolating the impact of multimodal fusion. It directly addresses whether combining RNA and image features improves performance, a critical design choice with high uncertainty.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation (config_006, config_032) and scvi_n200 RNA encoder (config_005, config_006) perform well. This experiment tests whether switching from concat to weighted fusion (while keeping transformer aggregation) in the top-performing config_032 improves accuracy. It isolates the effect of fusion method, a critical design choice, with minimal changes to the proven-effective architecture.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion yield high performance (config_033: 0.713 accuracy). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a stronger image encoder) maintains or improves performance, isolating the impact of image representation. This addresses uncertainty about the optimal image encoder choice while building on the promising multimodal framework.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_039) achieve the highest accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 (used in config_039) with scgpt (a more complex encoder) improves performance further. It isolates the effect of RNA encoder choice while keeping other critical components (image encoder, aggregation, fusion) consistent, addressing uncertainty about whether more complex RNA representations benefit this setup.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_039) achieve the highest accuracy (0.7249). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 (used in config_039) with pca_n2000 (which underperforms in singleprofile setups) affects performance, isolating the RNA encoder's impact. It balances exploitation (building on the multimodal/multiprofile success) and exploration (testing a key design choice with sparse evidence).
